observation.initial_state: A ballet dancer stands barefoot on a light studio floor, back to the camera, facing a wall of mirrors; her right arm hangs straight at her side and her left arm is raised in a high diagonal, hand well above head level. The mirror shows a matching frontal reflection of the same figure (not a second person). Framed pictures and the mirror seams sit at fixed positions, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: Early (frames 1-10): the raised left arm holds a high diagonal with the hand near the top of the frame, only minor positional variation; the hanging right arm and the legs/feet remain fixed.
Middle (frames 15-25): the left hand begins a slow downward arc about the shoulder, the arm angle opening toward more horizontal while the body stays planted.

Late (frames 30-41): the descent continues clearly, the left hand dropping to roughly shoulder height and the arm reaching a near-horizontal position; in the reflection the gaze/head follows the hand downward.

Throughout, the motion is rotation of one limb about the shoulder (an arc of the hand), not translation of the body and not a change in limb length; the mirror image tracks the real arm in lockstep, confirming reflection rather than a separate moving object.
observation.final_state: Dancer still standing in the same spot with right arm at her side; the left arm has lowered from the high diagonal to about shoulder height, nearly horizontal, hand at shoulder level. Background and camera framing unchanged.
uncertain_details: Small hand-height fluctuation between the earliest frames is within noise and not treated as real motion.
Exact head/neck tilt is hard to judge from the back view; only the reflection suggests a gaze shift.
Camera is assumed static because mirror seams and wall pictures do not move, but no independent depth cue confirms it.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
The images are chronological samples of the exact training clip, not its full source video.
Describe visible initial state, changes over the sequence, final state, and important unchanged
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"initial_state":"...", "visible_changes":["chronological observation with early/middle/late evidence"],
"final_state":"...", "uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English.
